# Abacus.AI Security Policy

Protecting your data is one of our most important responsibilities, and we're committed to being transparent about how we do it.

[Submit Compliance Request](https://abacus.ai/compliance-request) [Data Protection Addendum](https://static.abacus.ai/security/Abacus_dpa.pdf)

Security questions: [security@abacus.ai](mailto:security@abacus.ai)

Overview

## Standards and frameworks

Our compliance program aligns with globally recognized security and privacy standards and frameworks.

- ![SOC 2 Type II badge](https://abacus.ai/static/h61838edc/imgs/compliance/soc2-badge.webp)

### SOC 2 Type II


Security, availability and confidentiality controls

- ![ISO/IEC 27001 badge](https://abacus.ai/static/h95dabe48/imgs/compliance/iso27001-badge.webp)

### ISO/IEC 27001


Information security management system

- ![HIPAA badge](https://abacus.ai/static/he93ddd9f/imgs/compliance/hipaa-badge.webp)

### HIPAA


Safeguards for protected health information

- ![CCPA badge](https://abacus.ai/static/h112a23c9/imgs/compliance/ccpa-badge.webp)

California Consumer Privacy Act


Controls · 01

## Governance

A risk-driven program of administrative, technical and physical safeguards aligned with applicable requirements, standards and best practices, governed by an Information Security Committee led by our CISO.

- ### Information Security Committee



Cross-functional management representatives meet regularly to advise, prioritize and enable the Information Security Program, and collaborate on reviewing and managing risk.

- ### Reviewed policies



A full suite of security policies, reviewed, updated and approved on a predefined schedule.

- ### Defense in depth



Risk management is the foundation: periodic industry-standard risk assessments identify, analyze, monitor and respond to risk.

- ### Many sources of input



Vulnerability assessments, penetration tests and other reviews capture the full security posture. Risk treatments are planned and prioritized with key stakeholders to align with security and business objectives.


Controls · 02

## People

New staff are background-checked, and all employees and contractors are trained in security throughout their tenure.

- ### Background checks



Education, previous employment and internal and external references are verified before onboarding. Where local law permits, criminal, credit, immigration and security checks may follow, depending on the position.

- ### Security training



At orientation and throughout tenure. New employees read and agree to the Acceptable Use Policy and Code of Conduct.

- ### Role-based training



The security team teaches new engineers secure coding, product design and automated vulnerability testing tools.

- ### Threat awareness



Training also covers phishing, ransomware and social engineering.


Controls · 03

## Operations

Least-privilege access, continuous monitoring and a highly redundant platform.

- ### Access management



Least privilege and need-to-know by role. All staff use MFA; production is reached only through a bastion host with unique SSH keys and token 2FA. All staff also use strong passwords. Automated daily review, manual recertification at least quarterly.

- ### Vulnerability management



Periodic third-party scans with commercial tools, automated and manual penetration testing, QA, software security reviews and external audits. Findings are logged, prioritized by severity and owned until remediated. Bug bounties for vulnerabilities disclosed by external parties.

- ### Malware prevention



We prevent, detect and eradicate malware, with anti-malware on all corporate laptops and servers. Safe Browsing is required in Chrome.

- ### Customer access control



Built-in login or SAML 2.0 single sign-on with multi-factor authentication. Customers create and manage their own users, assign privileges and limit access to their data. Access attempts are logged for review.

- ### Monitoring and alerting



Automated alerts on application attacks, error rates and abuse, with traffic blocking, process termination and quarantine at predefined thresholds. Build procedures are fully automated.

- ### Data center security



Layered physical security at AWS and other data centers: electronic access cards, alarms, vehicle barriers, perimeter fencing, metal detectors, biometrics and laser intrusion detection. 24/7 cameras with access logs, background-checked guards on patrol, secure hardware disposal, redundant power and environmental controls.

- ### High availability



Data replicated synchronously across geographically distributed data centers, with automatic failover. 99.95% uptime with no scheduled downtime or maintenance windows. Hardened, stripped-down operating systems, with resources allocated dynamically to demand.

- ### Backups and recovery



Daily encrypted backups in the local region, kept for seven days for every database. Monitored, with failure alerts escalated, investigated and resolved, and periodically tested for recovery.


Controls · 04

## Data security and ownership

Customers own and control their data. It is encrypted, separated, tightly accessed and deleted on schedule.

- ### Customers own their data



You keep full ownership of your inputs and outputs, and complete control over how long your data is retained.

- ### No training on your data



Your data only trains models you specifically request, such as fine-tuning on your proprietary data. Those models are owned exclusively by you.

- ### Prompts never train an LLM



Your prompts, queries and responses are not used to train a large language model.

- ### Encryption



AES-256 at rest, TLS 1.2 or higher in transit, one-way hashed passwords. Standard protocols and algorithms only. TLS certificates are renewed annually.

- ### Key management



Keys live in AWS KMS and rotate by data sensitivity. Customer-supplied keys are not supported today.

- ### Data segregation



Logically separated by a unique key, or isolated databases on request. Separate production, staging and development environments, with no production data in lower environments.

- ### Just-in-time access



Access is limited to employees with a specific business need, and we try to troubleshoot without it. When it is needed, it is requested for a limited time, logged, monitored and revoked automatically. No customer data persists on employee laptops, and all access ends the moment someone leaves.

- ### Audit trails



Every infrastructure change and every access to customer data is logged. Only a few senior engineers can reach production.

- ### Employee authentication



A password manager for every employee. Production is shielded by network isolation, SSH keys with passphrases, VPN and two-factor authentication.

- ### Retention and deletion



Data is deleted within 30 days of cancellation. Deletion requests can be processed the same day.


Controls · 05

## Application

Features are reviewed for security from conception, and every code change is peer-reviewed and tested.

- ### Secure development lifecycle



Version-controlled code, peer review and CI on every change. Repository access needs strong credentials and 2FA.

- ### Secure by design



Senior engineers review features at conception. CSP and security headers guard against XSS, clickjacking and injection.

- ### Security testing



Internal testing follows the OWASP Testing Guide, and top-tier third parties independently verify our applications.

- ### Release management



New code is proposed, approved, merged and deployed thousands of times a day. Every production change is logged and archived, the engineering team is alerted automatically, and releases cause no downtime. Major changes are announced through web messages and product update posts.


Controls · 06

## Network and vendors

Only explicitly authorized traffic gets in, and every supplier is assessed before onboarding.

- ### Web Application Firewall



Allows only explicitly authorized ingress traffic.

- ### Intrusion Prevention System



Detects and blocks anomalous traffic patterns, including DDoS attacks.

- ### Vendor assessment



Suppliers are assessed for security and privacy practices proportionate to their access before onboarding.

- ### Contractual terms



Suppliers sign security, confidentiality and privacy terms. Sub-processors are listed in our DPA.


Controls · 07

## Privacy

Our customers operate across regulated industries, and our Information Security Committee continuously monitors and responds to changes.

- ### Never sold



As our privacy policy states, personal data is never sold to third parties.

- ### Privacy by design



Customer needs and privacy considerations guide how our products are designed and built. Our protections keep data unaltered and private, and best practices, customer needs and regulatory requirements are built into our privacy program.

- ### Regulatory alignment



Our program aligns with SOC 2 Type II, ISO/IEC 27001, HIPAA, GDPR and CCPA.

- ### Data Protection Officer



Reach our Data Protection Officer, Ajit Deshpande, at dpo@abacus.ai.


FAQ

## Frequently asked questions

Do you train models on our data?

No, except models you specifically ask for, such as fine-tuning on your own data. Those models are owned exclusively by you, and your prompts, queries and responses are never used to train a large language model.

Where is our data stored?

On AWS, Microsoft Azure or Google Cloud in the USA region you choose. We do not move customer data between regions.

How is our data separated from other customers?

Logically, by a unique key in our databases. If you need more stringent separation, we can set up isolated databases.

Can we use our own encryption keys?

Not at this time. Encryption keys are managed in AWS KMS.

Do you support single sign-on?

Yes. Built-in login or SAML 2.0 single sign-on, with multi-factor authentication. You create and manage your own users and their privileges, and access attempts are logged.

What happens to our data if we cancel?

We retain data for up to 30 days after cancellation or termination, then securely delete it. Deletion requests can be processed the same day.
